name: OSIRIS-REx
first: Largest asteroid sample ever returned (121.6 g of Bennu, delivered to Earth 2023-09-24)
description: OSIRIS-REx carried out one of the most exacting asteroid-proximity operations ever attempted. Launched 2016-09-08 from Cape Canaveral on an Atlas V 411, used a 2017 Earth gravity assist to rotate its orbital plane onto Bennu's 6° inclination, and rendezvoused with the 492-m carbonaceous near-Earth asteroid 2018-12-03. After stationkeeping at ~19 km, it later entered a record ~1.4 km orbit — the closest spacecraft orbit ever around any celestial body. Spent two years mapping Bennu's boulder-strewn surface and discovering active particle ejections. 2020-10-20 the Touch-and-Go sample arm descended to the Nightingale site, fired N₂ gas into the surface, and grabbed a plume — sinking 50 cm into a 'rubble-pile fluid' surface. Sample Return Capsule delivered 121.6 g of Bennu material to Utah 2023-09-24. The spacecraft itself was immediately redesignated OSIRIS-APEX, en route to a 2029 Apophis rendezvous.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: Atlas V 411 from Cape Canaveral SLC-41.

events.label: EARTH GRAVITY ASSIST
events.note: 2017-09-22, 17,237 km over Antarctica — rotates orbital plane onto Bennu's 6° inclination.

events.label: BENNU RENDEZVOUS
events.note: Arrives at Bennu; stationkeeps at ~19 km then progressively tightens to a record ~1.4 km orbit — closest spacecraft orbit ever around any celestial body.

events.label: TAG SAMPLE COLLECTION
events.note: 2020-10-20. Touch-and-Go arm sinks 50 cm into the rubble-pile surface; grabs 121.6 g.

events.label: SAMPLE RETURN
events.note: 2023-09-24. SRC parachutes into Utah Test and Training Range; spacecraft becomes OSIRIS-APEX.
